summary: Strong file. I checked every financial_model input against its cited source: the CareScout $40/h CA non-medical caregiver median and the $91,520 homemaker figure; DHCS PCS and Respite $29/$33/$38 with the $15 wage assumption; the IHSS Aug-2026 county wages (SD $20.40, LA $19.64, SF $23.00); 930,755 recipients, 843,828 providers and 119.0 h; BLS OEWS 2025 metro wages for 31-1122, 11-9151, 39-1022 and 43-6013; the $16.90 state minimum and the local minimums; EDD UI/ETT/SDI; FTB LLC tiers; SOS fees; the HCO fee of $5,603; HCA $35; the DHCS $750 CY2026 fee; the IRS 72.5 cents; and the CDI $1.65 benchmark. All match. The model recomputes exactly (pp75 +27,386 / 0.526; mix60 +15,405 / 0.571; pp40 +9,057 / 0.668; pp20 +3,909 / 0.70; pchs100 -9,032 / 1.185). Every sensitivity figure in financial_narrative and risks reproduces, as do the ramp figures (pp40 cumulative deficit about $124,911, first profitable month 11). LLC-fee tiers are sized correctly for each configuration. Rent is fixed. Staffing satisfies the statute, which sets no ratios. Licensing facts are verified against HCS 281, HSC 1796.12/.17/.37/.42/.43/.45/.49 and SB 412 ch. 414: $1M/$3M, workers' comp, the $10k bond with third-party coverage, the 60-day renewal notice, TB at 90 days before / 7 days after, training of 2h+3h then 5h, and dementia training from 1/1/2027. HCO counts were recomputed from the CHHS CSV (2,247 / 210 / 1,197; LA 594, Orange 244, SD 230; 433 first licensed in 2024, 283 closed). Contacts (HCSB, CPMB, HCBA, DHCS pricing inbox) are verified. Only a source-id error and small wording or advisory issues remain. Several FindLaw/Justia/eCFR/DOL URLs return 403 to curl, but they load in a browser fetcher and contain the claims.

issues.evidence: The 'Medi-Cal provider application fee' startup line ($0-$750) cites S43, which is 42 U.S.C. 1396b(l) (the EVV statute). That source says nothing about the fee. The DHCS Application Fees page (S20) states the fee is $750 for applications submitted 1/1/2026-12/31/2026, and that physician/NPP groups and individuals are exempt.
issues.fix: Change source_id to "S20" and change '[S43]' in that line's notes to '[S20]'.

issues.current: No mention of the ACA employer mandate; benefits are 4% of payroll.
issues.evidence: IRS: an employer is an ALE if it has at least 50 full-time employees, including full-time equivalents. Part-time hours are summed, capped at 120 per person, and divided by 120. At 90% census, pp75 and pchs100 each schedule 5,670 caregiver hours a month (67.5 × 84 and 90 × 63). That is 5,670 ÷ 120 ≈ 47 FTE before counting 5 full-time office staff, so about 52 FTE. Both would be ALEs subject to IRC 4980H (offer affordable coverage to full-time employees, or pay a penalty if a full-time employee gets a premium tax credit). pp40 (~28 FTE) and mix60 (~38 FTE) are below the threshold.
issues.fix: Add a risk bullet: 'At about 75 private-pay clients or 100 PCHS members, the agency reaches roughly 50 full-time-equivalent employees (ACA applicable large employer). It must then offer affordable health coverage to full-time (30+ h/week) staff or face IRC 4980H penalties. The 4% benefits load does not cover this; get a quote, or keep most aides under 30 hours a week.' Leave the model unchanged; the premium amount is unverifiable.
